statements.says: The commercial-lease provisions apply to leases of buildings or premises in which a business is run by a registered trader, industrialist, craftsman or craft enterprise.
Included: leases of annexed premises or buildings necessary to run the business, owned by the owner of the business or main building.
Included: leases of bare land on which commercial, industrial or craft buildings were built before or after the lease, if built or used with the owner's express consent.
The provisions also apply to leases granted to communes for municipal services and to premises needed by public economic enterprises, provided public property is not affected.
They also apply, subject to articles 185 and 186, to premises owned by the State, wilayas, communes or public bodies that meet article 169 and paragraphs 1 and 2 of article 170.
Exception: the provisions do not apply to temporary work permits granted by the administration for a building it had already acquired after a declaration of public utility.

Exception: the provisions do not apply to monopoly leases except for rent revision; they do apply to long-term leases in the cases of articles 169 and 170 provided sub-tenant renewal does not extend occupation beyond the end of the long lease.

Only tenants, transferees or successors who prove they ran the business themselves or through employees for two consecutive years under one or more registered leases, or four consecutive years under successive oral or written leases, may claim renewal.
A lease under these provisions ends only by notice to quit, given according to local custom and at least six months before the term.
If no notice to quit is given, a written lease continues by tacit extension beyond the term fixed in the contract.

A lease subject to a condition allowing the lessor to seek rescission ends only by a notice given six months before the term, in the customary period, and it must refer to the contractual condition having occurred.
For multi-stage leases, notice to quit must follow the paragraph 1 periods if the lessor ends the lease at the end of a stage.
Notice to quit must be by extrajudicial act, state its reasons and restate the content of article 194, or it is void.
Where no notice to quit is given, a tenant wanting renewal must apply in the six months before the lease ends or, if applicable, at any time during its extension.

The renewal request is notified to the lessor by extrajudicial act (valid to a manager with sufficient capacity; one of several owners binds all) and must include the content of the paragraph set out after it, or it is void.
The lessor has three months from notification of the renewal request to state personally whether it refuses, with reasons; silence is consent to renewal in principle.
The refusal notice must restate article 194, or it is void.

A renewed lease lasts as long as the expired one but not more than nine years unless agreed otherwise, and runs from the end of the previous lease or the date of renewal; a lessor who withdraws a refusal renews from notification of acceptance.

The lessor may refuse renewal but, except for the exceptions of article 177 onwards, must pay the evicted tenant an eviction compensation equal to the damage caused, including the commercial value of the business and moving and re-installation costs.
Exception: the lessor may refuse renewal without compensation if it proves a serious and legitimate reason against the tenant.

A breach of obligation or stopping of business may be relied on only if it continued or recurred more than one month after a warning, itself an extrajudicial act stating the reason and the content of the paragraph, or it is void.
Exception: no compensation if the building is wholly or partly demolished as uninhabitable or cannot be occupied without danger; the tenant has priority in the rebuilt building.

The lessor may refuse renewal to rebuild, but must pay eviction compensation unless it offers a suitable premises in a similar place; the tenant then has three months to accept by extrajudicial act or sue under article 197.

To use the priority right the tenant must notify the owner by extrajudicial act on leaving or within the next three months; the owner offers a new lease; the tenant has three months to respond or sue; the owner who does not comply may owe damages.
The owner may delay renewal up to three years to raise the building, with compensation equal to the damage but not more than three years' rent.

The lessor may refuse renewal for annexed residential premises for personal or family housing, with conditions and exceptions, and must occupy within six months for at least six years, failing which the tenant keeps proportional eviction compensation.
The recovery right applies to land under article 169 paragraph 2 only for the part needed for building, with article 178 if commercial activity must stop.

An owner or principal tenant who is lessor and also seller of the business and received the full price cannot refuse renewal without paying eviction compensation, unless there is a serious or legitimate reason.
State, wilaya, commune or public-body lessors must pay eviction compensation on refusing renewal even for public utility.
If the lessor used its rights only to fraudulently defeat the tenant's rights, the tenant is owed compensation equal to the damage.
A tenant entitled to eviction compensation cannot be forced to leave before receiving it and may stay on the expired lease's terms.

In the article 178 paragraph 2 case the tenant must leave once the provisional compensation set by the court president is paid; premises are handed over after fifteen days from payment, or to a judicial custodian.
Leases concluded from the date of publication of this law in the Official Gazette must be in official form on pain of nullity, for a term freely set by the parties.
For such leases the tenant must leave at the end of the term with no notice to quit and no entitlement to eviction compensation, unless the parties agreed otherwise.
Renewal of leases concluded before that publication stays subject to the legislation in force at the date the lease was made.

Rent revision is requested by extrajudicial act or registered letter stating the rent claimed or offered (on pain of nullity); after three months without agreement the interested party sues; new rent is due from the request date.
A revision request is allowed only after three years from start of operation or of the renewed lease, and a new one every three years.
If no agreement at the end of three months from notification, disputes on application of this chapter go to the competent court of the building's location by summons.

If the tenant claims eviction compensation, the interested party may go to the urgent-matters president for an expert, before the three-month period ends; the expert report is filed within two months.

If the lessor accepts renewal but disputes rent, term or conditions, the parties appear before the president of the court of the building's location, who rules by reasoned order in the urgent-matters procedure.
During the case the tenant keeps paying the old rent (or the provisional rent); if no agreement within one month of notification of the final judgment, the order or judgment counts as the lease.

A tenant contesting a refusal of renewal or seeking eviction compensation sues the lessor before the court of the building's location, the summons being served within three months of notification of the refusal.

A lessor who lost may avoid compensation within fifteen days of the judgment becoming final (or of the appeal judgment) by paying costs and accepting renewal, unless the tenant has left or leased or bought another building.
All actions under this chapter, except those of articles 196 and 197, are brought before the court of the building's location and are subject to limitation after two years.
Clauses that remove the right to renewal are void, notably the provisions of articles 191 to 193.

priorSteps.requiredWhen: For a lease under articles 169 to 171 made before the 187 مكرر date, to end it at term: notice by extrajudicial act at least six months before the term, with reasons and restating article 194; also to refuse renewal.
notRequiredWhen: Lease concluded from the date of publication of the law in the Official Gazette (187 مكرر): the tenant leaves at the end of the term with no notice, unless the parties agreed otherwise
priorSteps.sanctionIfMissing: Notice without reasons or without article 194 is void (173 ¶5); with no notice, a written lease continues by tacit extension (173 ¶2)

priorSteps.requiredWhen: The tenant wants renewal when no notice to quit was given: request by extrajudicial act in the six months before the end of the lease, containing the paragraph set out in the text.
priorSteps.sanctionIfMissing: Request lacking the required paragraph is void (174 ¶3); a refusal lacking article 194 is void (174 ¶5)

priorSteps.requiredWhen: To rely on a breach or stopping of the business as a serious and legitimate reason without compensation: an extrajudicial warning stating the reason and the content of the paragraph, then one month with no end to the breach.
For a rescission clause for non-payment of rent to take effect: notice to pay stating the one-month period.
priorSteps.sanctionIfMissing: The clause has no effect until a month has passed after the unanswered notice

priorSteps.requiredWhen: Before suing on a lease dispute under this chapter: three months from notification without agreement.
notRequiredWhen: Eviction compensation claimed: the urgent-matters president may be seized for an expert before the three months end (194 ¶2)

priorSteps.requiredWhen: Before a rent revision case: request by extrajudicial act or registered letter stating the rent claimed or offered, then three months without agreement.
priorSteps.sanctionIfMissing: Nullity if the rent claimed or offered is not stated

territory.rule: The court in whose area the building is located
territory.when: Disputes on the application of the commercial-lease chapter, renewal refusal, eviction compensation and rent terms

openPoints.question: Which contracts fall under the pre-reform regime and which under the post-reform regime, and by what date?
readings: The texts use the date of publication of the amending law in the Official Gazette, but that date is not given here (Law 05-02 text missing); the date cannot be fixed from these texts
A contract on or after that date is under 187 مكرر (official form, free term, no notice, no compensation); a contract before it keeps the older regime for its renewal (187 مكرر 1)

openPoints.question: Does 187 مكرر 1 give only the renewal to the old law, or also the notice to quit and the compensation?
readings: Notice to quit and eviction compensation follow the same law as a necessary consequence

openPoints.question: Is the six-month notice to quit period counted by calendar months, and who raises its non-compliance?
readings: The texts give no counting rule and no raiser
Customary local practice may apply (173 ¶1 refers to local custom)

openPoints.question: Is the three-month period of 197 ¶3 a forfeiture or a procedural period, and does the two-year limit of 198 ¶1 run from a stated event?
readings: 197 ¶3 states no sanction; 198 ¶1 excludes actions under 196 and 197 and states no starting event
Two years from the event giving rise to the action

openPoints.question: What must the article 194 restatement and the paragraph of 174 ¶3 contain?
readings: 174 ¶3 refers to a paragraph inserted after it that is not reproduced here

openPoints.question: Which section of the court hears a commercial lease case?
readings: Real-estate section (lease of professional premises is a real-property matter)
Civil or commercial section; the texts do not say

openPoints.question: Does 197 ¶3 refer to the notice period of 173 or to the refusal of renewal of 174 ¶4?
readings: Any refusal notified by the lessor, including by notice to quit
